mirror.1: After the failure, you flood yourself with promises that everything changes now.
mirror.2: You give until you are empty, then keep score against yourself for not being further along.
mirror.3: You promise yourself that life starts when you lose the weight or get the promotion.
mirror.4: You leave the habit, then pull yourself back with "maybe it wasn't that bad."
mirror.5: The voice inside says you are not enough, and it was installed by the systems you lived in.
mirror.6: You tell yourself "it wasn't that bad" while your body still remembers that it was.
mirror.7: You rest and feel guilty, then work and feel resentful, so both choices punish you.
mirror.8: You feel good about yourself one day and worthless the next, with nothing in between changed.
mirror.9: You achieve the thing, and the next goal appears before you can feel it was enough.
mirror.10: You tell yourself "I'm fine" and "it is what it is," so nothing ever has to change.
mirror.11: You call the coworker "lazy" because you are terrified of your own need for rest.
mirror.12: You name the harm, then attack yourself for being dramatic and playing the victim.
mirror.13: The exhaustion and the loneliness are no longer alarming, because you normalized them.
mirror.14: You cancel the plan and let the friendship go quiet so no one gets close enough to leave.
mirror.15: You compare yourself to a stranger on the feed whose life looks like the one you should have.
mirror.16: When you are about to set a boundary, your mother's voice in your head says "that's selfish."
mirror.17: You tell the story of your own life with the system's edits, and you are always the problem.
mirror.18: The grief arrives and you scroll, ignoring your own body's signals.
mirror.19: You point to "I chose this" as proof that everything that followed was wanted.
mirror.20: You return to your own suffering because it is the most familiar thing in your life.
mirror.21: You tell yourself "I can't change" because every system punished your attempts to try.
mirror.22: You restrict the food and override the exhaustion, then call the control discipline.
mirror.23: You Google the answer before you check what your own body already knows.
mirror.24: Strip away the job title and the roles, and you are not sure who is left.
mirror.25: You say "it happened for a reason" to avoid feeling what actually happened to you.
mirror.26: You tell yourself "I can't afford to rest" and deny yourself even the small things.
mirror.27: You wait until the deadline becomes an emergency, because only a crisis lets you change.
mirror.28: You stop mentioning the book you were going to write, and no one mourns the dream.
mirror.29: You replace yourself with another diet and another plan instead of becoming whole.
mirror.30: You tell yourself "I'm just tired" so you never have to see the pattern you are in.

body.1: Your shoulders drop, your jaw unclenches, and the body opens before the mind can judge.
body.2: The gift lands as a heaviness in the shoulders, as if something was placed on you.
body.3: The breath stays high in the chest as the body leans toward a future that never comes.
body.4: A lurch in the chest pulls you back, the same craving an addict feels for what they quit.
body.5: The chest caves in and the throat tightens, as if your voice is being taken.
body.6: Your jaw clenches and the ground feels unstable when something is wrong but cannot be named.
body.7: Your body feels stuck, unable to move forward or back, with nowhere for the pressure to go.
body.8: Your body cannot settle, scanning every notification for the next reward.
body.9: Your limbs feel heavy after the goal is reached, because enough is never enough.
body.10: Your brow furrows and your head feels foggy, sure you missed something that was never said.
body.11: Your face flushes and your chest tightens as you brace against the blame.
body.12: Within five seconds you move from confusion to fear to shame to apologizing for being hurt.
body.13: You feel nothing where you should feel something, because the alarm was slowly drained.
body.14: Your hands go cold and your chest feels hollow where the connection used to live.
body.15: Your stomach drops with the fear of being replaced while your eyes scan for the rival.
body.16: Your throat tightens when someone you love repeats the system's words to you.
body.17: Your face burns and your body cannot sit still with the feeling of being talked about.
body.18: A low ache behind the sternum stays, and the words in your throat have no one to receive them.
body.19: Your hand trembles and the pen feels heavy as you rush to sign and move on.
body.20: Your body relaxes only near the person who hurts you, because it was trained to the swing.
body.21: Your limbs feel weighted and getting out of bed feels like a physical feat.
body.22: The care feels like an embrace too tight to breathe inside.
body.23: Your body shrinks and your hand reaches for the phone the moment you must decide alone.
body.24: You feel like you are performing your life behind a mask you can no longer take off.
body.25: The calm floats in your head and upper chest and never settles into the belly.
body.26: A knot forms in your stomach the moment you open the bank app.
body.27: Your heart pounds and your vision narrows until waiting feels dangerous.
body.28: The chest ache is not cardiac but feels fatal, and the body is too heavy to move.
body.29: A cold feeling settles in your center as you watch someone else receive your warmth.
body.30: A background hum of unease stays in your body, carrying a truth it cannot prove.
